## Audio

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Audio
```

Audio levels and short sounds (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`,
"Audio"). A client-only platform interface: [`BrowserAudio`](#browseraudio) is
injected with no `use` rule, and [`k.test.TestAudio`](k-test.md#testaudio) replaces it in
tests.

**Members**

- `func meter(for stream: MediaStream, lifetime: CaptureLifetime = .owner) throws AudioError -> AudioMeter`
  Measures the loudness of `stream`'s sound. It reads `0.0` until the
  first user's action on the page, when browsers let audio start.

  - Throws: [`AudioError.noTrack`](#audioerror) for a stream without audio,
    `.unsupported` where Web Audio is missing.
- `func play(_ source: MediaSource) async throws PlaybackError`
  Plays a short sound without an element, and resolves when it ends.

## AudioCapture

```k,ignore
public struct AudioCapture implements Equatable
```

How to capture a microphone.

**Members**

- `let device: MediaDeviceId? = nil`
  The microphone; `nil` is the browser's default. A chosen device is
  exact: when it is gone the capture throws `.notFound`.
- `let echoCancellation: Bool = true`
  Removes the speakers' sound from the microphone's.
- `let noiseSuppression: Bool = true`
  Removes steady background noise.
- `let autoGainControl: Bool = true`
  Keeps the level steady.

## AudioError

```k,ignore
public enum AudioError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why a meter couldn't be made.

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  This browser has no Web Audio.
- `case noTrack`
  The stream has no audio track.

## AudioMeter

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class AudioMeter
```

The loudness of a stream's sound. Its fields are reactive.

**Members**

- `var level: Double`
  The loudness now, `0.0...1.0` (RMS on a perceptual scale), updated
  at most 30 times a second.
- `var peak: Double`
  The highest `level` of the last 1.5 seconds.
- `var isSpeaking: Bool`
  Whether `level` has been above the speech threshold for 150 ms.
- `func waveform(points: Int) -> List<Double>`
  A snapshot of the last 50 ms, `points` values in `-1.0...1.0`, for
  drawing as an SVG polyline.
- `func stop()`
  Stops measuring.

## CaptureError

```k,ignore
public enum CaptureError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why a capture failed (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Errors").

**Members**

- `case unsupported`
  No capture here: an insecure origin, a browser without it, or a
  permissions policy.
- `case notAsked`
  The permission is `.prompt`: call `requestAccess(for:)` from a
  user's action first.
- `case denied`
  The user or the system refused.
- `case cancelled`
  The screen picker was closed without a choice.
- `case notFound`
  No device of the kind, or the chosen one is gone.
- `case busy`
  Another application holds the device.
- `case unsatisfiable(setting: String)`
  The device can't do what was asked; `setting` names the constraint.

## CaptureRequest

```k,ignore
public enum CaptureRequest implements Equatable
```

What a capture opens (`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Requests"):
a request for nothing can't be written.

**Members**

- `case audio(AudioCapture)`
  A microphone.
- `case video(VideoCapture)`
  A camera.
- `case audioAndVideo(AudioCapture, VideoCapture)`
  A microphone and a camera, asked for in one prompt.
- `static let microphone: CaptureRequest = .audio(AudioCapture())`
  The default microphone, with echo cancellation, noise suppression
  and automatic gain.
- `static let camera: CaptureRequest = .video(VideoCapture())`
  The default camera.
- `static let cameraAndMicrophone: CaptureRequest = .audioAndVideo(AudioCapture(), VideoCapture())`
  The default camera and microphone.

## MediaController

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class MediaController
```

Drives one `video` or `audio` element from code
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "MediaController"):
`audio(source: .file(memo.file)).controller(player)`. Its fields are
reactive. Giving it to a second element is a run-time error naming
both.

**Members**

- `init()`
  Creates a controller driving no element yet.
- `var state: PlaybackState`
  `.idle` until its element has a source, then what it does.
- `var currentTime: Duration`
  The position; reactive.
- `var duration: Duration?`
  The length; `nil` until known, and for live streams.
- `var volume: Double`
  The volume, `0.0...1.0`.
- `func play() async throws PlaybackError`
  Starts playing.

  - Throws: [`PlaybackError.blocked`](#playbackerror) when the browser wants a user's
    action first, `.unsupportedFormat` or `.unreachable`.
- `func pause()`
  Pauses.
- `func toggle() async`
  Plays when paused, and pauses when playing. A refused play leaves
  the state `.blocked`.
- `func seek(to time: Duration)`
  Moves the position.
- `func setVolume(_ volume: Double)`
  Sets `volume`, clamped to `0.0...1.0`.

## MediaDevices

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface MediaDevices
```

The camera, the microphone and the screen
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Capture"). A client-only platform
interface: [`BrowserMediaDevices`](#browsermediadevices) is injected with no `use` rule, and
[`k.test.TestMediaDevices`](k-test.md#testmediadevices) replaces it in tests.

Only `requestAccess(for:)` prompts for the camera or the microphone,
and only from a user's action. `capture(_:lifetime:)` never prompts:
while the kind's permission is `.prompt` it throws
[`CaptureError.notAsked`](#captureerror).

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  Whether this browser can capture here: `false` outside a secure
  context (`http:` on a host other than `localhost`), and during
  server rendering.
- `var cameraPermission: PermissionState`
  Whether the app may use the camera. Reactive; `.prompt` during
  server rendering.
- `var microphonePermission: PermissionState`
  Whether the app may use the microphone. Reactive; `.prompt` during
  server rendering.
- `var devices: List<MediaDevice>`
  The microphones, cameras and speakers, refreshed when one is plugged
  in or removed and after a grant. Empty during server rendering and
  until the first enumeration, shortly after hydration.
- `@UserAction func requestAccess(for request: CaptureRequest) async -> PermissionState`
  Asks the user for every kind in `request` in one prompt, unless the
  permissions already say `.granted` or `.denied`.

  - Returns: `.granted` when every kind was granted, `.denied` when
    any was refused, `.prompt` when the user dismissed the prompt.
- `func capture(_ request: CaptureRequest, lifetime: CaptureLifetime = .owner) async throws CaptureError -> MediaStream`
  Opens the devices `request` names, without prompting.

  - Parameter lifetime: `.owner` stops the stream when the run that
    captured it is cancelled; `.service` when the injecting service's
    instance ends.
  - Throws: [`CaptureError.notAsked`](#captureerror) while a kind's permission is
    `.prompt`, `.denied`, `.notFound`, `.busy`, `.unsatisfiable` or
    `.unsupported`.
- `@UserAction func captureScreen(_ request: ScreenCapture = ScreenCapture(), lifetime: CaptureLifetime = .owner) async throws CaptureError -> MediaStream`
  Shows the browser's screen picker and captures what the user
  chooses. It is the request and the capture at once, so it is a
  user's action.

  - Throws: [`CaptureError.cancelled`](#captureerror) when the picker was closed
    without a choice, `.unsupported` where screens can't be captured.

## MediaSource

```k,ignore
public enum MediaSource
```

What a `video` or `audio` element plays
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Showing and playing media").

**Members**

- `case stream(MediaStream)`
  A live stream; a local one plays no sound unless `.monitor(true)`.
- `case file(File)`
  A file, such as a recording, through an object URL the element

- `case url(Url)`

## MediaStream

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class MediaStream implements Equatable
```

Live audio and video: what a capture returns
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Streams and tracks").

A handle, not a value: it isn't `Codable`, so it can't be stored, sent
in an rpc or put in a `@Load` field, and two streams are equal only
when they are the same stream. Its fields are reactive, like `@State`.
It stops with its owner (`CaptureLifetime`).

**Members**

- `var audioTracks: List<MediaTrack>`
  The audio tracks.
- `var videoTracks: List<MediaTrack>`
  The video tracks.
- `var isLive: Bool`
  Whether some track is still live.
- `var isLocal: Bool`
  Whether it was captured on this device, rather than received from a
  peer.
- `func stop()`
  Stops every track, which releases the devices. Stopping a stopped
  stream does nothing.

## MediaTrack

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class MediaTrack implements Equatable
```

One source of a [`MediaStream`](#mediastream): a microphone, a camera or a screen.
Its fields are reactive.

**Members**

- `var kind: TrackKind`
  `.audio` or `.video`.
- `var label: String`
  What the browser calls the source ("MacBook Pro Microphone").
- `var device: MediaDeviceId?`
  The device it came from; `nil` for a screen.
- `var isEnabled: Bool`
  The app's mute: a disabled track sends silence or black frames, and
  keeps the device open.
- `var isMuted: Bool`
  The source's mute: the system isn't delivering, through no action of
  the app.
- `var state: TrackState`
  `.live`, or `.ended` and why.
- `var settings: TrackSettings`
  The size, frame rate and audio settings the browser chose.
- `func setEnabled(_ enabled: Bool)`
  Enables or disables the track (`isEnabled`).
- `func stop()`
  Ends the track and, once no track uses it, releases the device.

## PlaybackState

```k,ignore
public enum PlaybackState implements Equatable
```

What a [`MediaController`](#mediacontroller)'s element is doing.

**Members**

## Recorder

```k,ignore
@Platform(side: .client)
public interface Recorder
```

Records a [`MediaStream`](#mediastream) to a file
(`docs/design/46-media-and-rtc.md`, "Recording"). A client-only
platform interface: [`BrowserRecorder`](#browserrecorder) is injected with no `use` rule,
and [`k.test.TestRecorder`](k-test.md#testrecorder) replaces it in tests.

**Members**

- `func start(_ stream: MediaStream, format: RecordingFormat, limit: RecordingLimit = RecordingLimit()) throws RecordingError -> RecordingSession`
  Starts recording `stream`. The session belongs to the stream's
  owner: it is stopped, and its data discarded, with the stream.

  - Parameters:
    - format: `.voice`, `.audio` and `.video` always work, in WebM or
      MP4 as the browser can; `.exact` names a media type.
    - limit: the recording stops by itself at this size or duration.
  - Throws: [`RecordingError.noTrack`](#recordingerror) when the stream has no track
    the format records, `.unsupportedFormat` for an `.exact` type the
    browser can't record.
- `func supports(_ format: RecordingFormat) -> Bool`
  Whether `format` can be recorded here; always `true` for the named
  formats.

## RecordingError

```k,ignore
public enum RecordingError implements Error, Equatable
```

Why a recording couldn't start or finish.

**Members**

- `case unsupportedFormat`
  The browser can't record this `.exact` media type.
- `case noTrack`
  The stream has no track the format records: `.voice` on a stream
  without audio.
- `case failed`
  The browser's encoder failed.

## RecordingFormat

```k,ignore
public enum RecordingFormat implements Equatable
```

What a recording is encoded as. The named formats try their WebM form,
then their MP4 form, so Chromium and Firefox record WebM and Safari
MP4.

**Members**

- `case voice`
  Speech: Opus at 32 kbps in WebM, else AAC in MP4.
- `case audio`
  Music: Opus at 128 kbps in WebM, else AAC in MP4.
- `case video`
  VP9 or VP8 with Opus in WebM, else H.264 with AAC in MP4; 2.5 Mbps.
- `case exact(mediaType: String, audioBitsPerSecond: Int?, videoBitsPerSecond: Int?)`
  Exactly this media type and these bit rates.

## RecordingLimit

```k,ignore
public struct RecordingLimit implements Equatable
```

Where a recording stops by itself. The default size is
`File.maximumSize`, 16 MiB, so every recording fits in a `File`.

**Members**

- `let size: Int = 16777216`
  The largest file, in bytes.
- `let duration: Duration? = nil`
  The longest recording; `nil` for none.

## RecordingSession

```k,ignore
@ClientOnly
public class RecordingSession
```

A recording in progress. Its fields are reactive.

**Members**

- `var state: RecordingState`
  `.recording`, `.paused`, or `.stopped` and why.
- `var elapsed: Duration`
  The time recorded, paused time excluded; updated each second.
- `var size: Int`
  The bytes recorded so far.
- `func pause()`
  Pauses the recording.
- `func resume()`
  Resumes a paused recording.
- `func stop(keepStream: Bool = false) async throws RecordingError -> Recording`
  Finishes the file and, unless `keepStream` is `true`, stops the
  stream. After the recording stopped by itself it returns everything
  recorded until then.

  - Throws: [`RecordingError.failed`](#recordingerror) when the browser's encoder
    failed.

```k,ignore

```

- `case stopped(RecordingStop)`


- `let noiseSuppression: Bool? = nil`
  Whether noise suppression is on.
- `let autoGainControl: Bool? = nil`
  Whether automatic gain is on.

## TrackState

```k,ignore
public enum TrackState implements Equatable
```

Whether a [`MediaTrack`](#mediatrack) still delivers.

**Members**

- `case live`
  It delivers.
- `case ended(TrackEnd)`
  It ended, for good.

## VideoCapture

```k,ignore
public struct VideoCapture implements Equatable
```

How to capture a camera. Sizes and frame rates are ideals: the browser
picks the nearest it can, and the track's `settings` say what it chose.

**Members**

- `let device: MediaDeviceId? = nil`
  The camera; `nil` is the browser's default. A chosen device is
  exact: when it is gone the capture throws `.notFound`.
- `let facing: CameraFacing? = nil`
  A phone's front (`.user`) or back (`.environment`) camera.
- `let size: VideoSize? = nil`
  The ideal size.
- `let frameRate: Int? = nil`
  The ideal frames per second.

```k,ignore
public struct VideoSize implements Equatable
```

A video's size in pixels.

**Members**

- `let width: Int`
  The width in pixels.
- `let height: Int`
  The height in pixels.
